item.title: Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr Jean Kaseya, has blamed a lack of international interest for the absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, saying the situation might have been different if the outbreak were affecting Western countries. Kaseya made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he called for greater African investment in vaccine research and manufacturing. He said, “I can tell you, if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccine will already be available. Why this vaccine today is not available? Because some of our partners decided to consider this issue as an African issue, they were not interested.” The Africa CDC chief, however, said the agency was taking steps to address the gap, including supporting clinical trials of vaccine candidates. He disclosed that an African manufacturer in Egypt was conducting clinical trials of a potential vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Kaseya also said the agency was working with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to explore clinical trials and compassionate use of Ervebo, a vaccine developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola. He stressed that the continent had the expertise and capacity to advance vaccine development, adding that Africa should not continue to depend solely on external partners during public health emergencies. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind. We have the knowledge, we have people with intelligence, we have capacity to manufacture vaccines, and we need to move on,” he said. Kaseya also called for greater domestic funding and improved coordination among African countries and international partners. He said 28 African countries had contributed funding to support the response to the current outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. The outbreak, declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, has caused more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities The disease has also been detected in other countries, with the Kenyan Health Ministry reporting a ninth case in the country on Tuesday, prompting concerns over cross-border transmission. Nigeria also confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20. The patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, is receiving medical care, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring. item.title: France reports first human Shamonda virus case, says no health risk
item.description: French health authorities said Thursday that the Shamonda virus, which usually affects livestock, had been detected in a human for the first time, in a severely immunocompromised patient who died earlier this month. There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement. It added that the human infection appeared to be “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient” hospitalised for a serious medical condition. “Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the ministries said. The virus, which belongs to the Orthobunyavirus group and is typically transmitted to animals by small biting insects, was first detected in Europe this summer, they said. At this stage in the investigation, the patient was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus was circulating in animals during the spring and summer, the ministries said. “The neurological complications observed in the immunocompromised patient prior to his death are very likely linked to infection with the Shamonda virus,” they added, citing preliminary findings. But “clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations are still ongoing”, they said. – In 14 European countries – The virus was first detected in Nigeria in the mid-1960s and has since been reported in cattle in several parts of Africa and in Japan. The virus was detected in Europe for the first time at the end of July, including on cattle farms in France. It has now been detected in 14 western European countries, according to an epidemiological bulletin from France’s national research institute monitoring animal health. Cattle are considered its main animal hosts, although sporadic infections in smaller livestock and horses have also been identified in France this summer. In cattle, the main symptoms are acute diarrhoea, fever, lethargy and a drop in milk production. An investigation is ongoing, and both the World Health Organization and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control have been notified. item.title: Who won Lagos in 2023?
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi of the Labour Party (LP) defeated Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Lagos State in the February 25, 2023, presidential election, overturning expectations in a state long regarded as Tinubu’s political stronghold. Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes, while Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) came third with 75,750 votes, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) received 8,442 votes. Obi won Lagos by 9,848 votes, making the result one of the major surprises of the 2023 presidential election. Tinubu, who governed Lagos from 1999 to 2007, had maintained significant political influence in the state through his party and political network. However, the result showed that his longstanding connection to Lagos did not guarantee victory at the polls. How Obi won Lagos According to the results published by INEC and reported by The Punch, Obi won nine of the state’s 20 local government areas, while Tinubu secured victories in the remaining 11. The Labour Party candidate performed strongly in Alimosho, Ojo, Oshodi-Isolo, Amuwo-Odofin, Eti-Osa, Ikeja, Kosofe, Somolu and Ajeromi-Ifelodun. In Alimosho, the state’s most populous local government area, Obi polled 71,327 votes against Tinubu’s 62,283. In Amuwo-Odofin, Obi recorded 55,547 votes, while Tinubu received 13,318. Obi also won Oshodi-Isolo with 51,020 votes against the APC candidate’s 27,181. Tinubu, meanwhile, won in areas including Agege, Apapa, Badagry, Epe, Ibeju-Lekki, Ifako-Ijaiye, Ikorodu, Lagos Island, Lagos Mainland, Mushin and Surulere. Despite winning more local government areas, Tinubu lost the overall contest because Obi accumulated more votes across the state. The result demonstrated the Labour Party’s ability to attract substantial support beyond the traditional structures of the APC and PDP. The outcome also reflected the appeal of Obi’s campaign among voters seeking an alternative to Nigeria’s established political parties, particularly young people who were prominent in the wider movement for political change. item.title: French city of Lyon bans ‘all protests’ on Saturday
item.description: Officials have banned “all protests” in France’s third-biggest city of Lyon on Saturday, ahead of nationwide demonstrations that day following rallies last weekend that descended into widespread street violence. The prefecture for the Rhone region said on Thursday in a statement to media that, “given the events of October 17, the prefect has decided to ban by decree all protests in the city of Lyon this Saturday, October 24”. Lyon, like Paris and other French cities, suffered clashes and looting when masked youths took to city centre streets on the sidelines of mass rallies protesting high inflation. The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, has said that his city experienced hours of “chaos” during the riots, with between 150 and 200 shops looted and a tourist office torched. Police arrested some 200 people. The organisers of the rallies, the Yellow Vest movement and unions, have called for another round of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living on Saturday, and a general strike and demonstrations on November 5. French officials who found themselves unable to contain last weekend’s violence this week ordered three nights of curfews in parts of Paris, Lyon and some other cities to protect shopping districts. item.title: Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo
item.description: Court is set to resume the trial of suspects linked to the abduction of 20 members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and others in Imo State. The suspects were apprehended in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Abia State during intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 by the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the military, police, and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang. The prospective corps members were abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, while they were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The gunmen attacked two buses conveying the prospective corps members and other passengers near Umunoha in the Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The victims were rescued on October 7 during a joint security operation at Amakohia-Ubi Village in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state. They were subsequently taken to the DSS hospital in Owerri for medical attention and necessary checks. During the search-and-rescue operation, the police had said their operatives located the kidnappers’ camp through drone surveillance but could not immediately advance because the location was reportedly planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Security agencies later intensified efforts to reach the victims and secure their release. item.title: Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN), Kaduna State Branch, has advised political parties to campaign virtually to minimise physical contact amid the Ebola outbreak. Mr Turman Benjamin, Chairman of the association in Kaduna gave the advice on Thursday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna. Benjamin recommended social media, text messages, telephone calls and virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Google Meet as alternatives to physical political rallies. He said the approach would reduce unnecessary contact and help minimise potential exposure while health authorities worked to contain the outbreak. Benjamin urged the Kaduna State Government to intensify public awareness, trace any contacts linked to the confirmed case and ensure adequate protective equipment for healthcare workers. He advised residents to avoid unnecessary physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, and observe appropriate hygiene measures. The medical laboratory scientist said Ebola could be transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons. He also urged the public to avoid handling the bodies of suspected or confirmed Ebola victims without appropriate training and protective equipment. Benjamin said only trained and properly equipped personnel should handle such bodies to reduce the risk of infection during burial preparations. He called on the government to provide hospitals with adequate personal protective equipment, including gloves and other appropriate protective gear. According to him, laboratory testing is essential to confirm Ebola because its early symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid fever. Benjamin further advised the public to exercise caution when handling or consuming wild animals that could carry infectious diseases. He urged the media to intensify public education on Ebola transmission, prevention and the importance of seeking prompt medical attention when symptoms develop. The chairman also called for vigilance among healthcare workers and members of the public, stressing the importance of early detection and effective infection prevention measures. The NAN reports that the Federal Government has confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring to prevent further transmission. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. The woman has since been placed in isolation and is receiving medical care, while health authorities have commenced contact tracing to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus.( NAN ) The post Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria – WHO
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the World Health Organization (WHO) saying there is no vaccine or specific treatment for the index Ebola virus case detected in Nigeria, which carried the Bundibugyo strain. Another headline features the Senate Committee on Public Accounts rejecting the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). Vanguard also reports that the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said only 108 out of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have survived the Federal Government’s rigorous screening for possible admission into tertiary institutions. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian’s lead headline states that weak oversight and fiscal plan have left over 6,000 projects abandoned across the country, with their combined value running into trillions of naira. The Punch reports that the diplomat diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has reportedly deteriorated into multi-organ failure, as the Federal Government and state governments intensify surveillance, contact tracing and emergency preparedness to prevent the spread of the deadly disease. Lastly, The Nation reports that Vice President Kashim Shettima challenged state governments to stop depending on the Federal Government for solutions to their electricity challenges. item.title: Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued four kidnapped victims during separate intelligence-led operations in Zamfara and Kebbi states as the military intensifies efforts to combat terrorism and kidnapping across the North West. According to the Army, the victims were rescued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State and between Bena and Sawade in Kebbi State. “In Zamfara, troops rescued Mansur Shehu, 25, and Kadijat Haruna, 49, following a response to a reported terrorist incident on farmland across a river in Binoni Marafa, Maru LGA. “In Kebbi, troops conducted a search-and-rescue operation after receiving reports of suspected terrorists moving with kidnapped victims from Dupindu Village, Kanya District, Danko-Wasagu LGA. “The operation secured the freedom of Jimoh Su-Arege, 35, and Kalahe Danjuma, 41, who were subsequently handed over to the Seriki of Dipindu. “The military said troops have continued to intensify patrols and surveillance across affected communities to strengthen security, dominate operational areas and deny criminal elements freedom of action. “The successful operations highlight Operation Fansan Yamma’s sustained efforts to rescue abducted persons, disrupt terrorist activities and restore peace across Zamfara and Kebbi states,” the military said. item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance. The affected pupils were rushed to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode; the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo; and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed pupils reportedly fainting and being rushed to hospitals following the incident. The state government had previously identified the substance as methane, although the precise source of the recurring emissions remains under investigation. A teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke to our correspondent on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 10am when pupils and staff began experiencing breathing difficulties, with some collapsing. “The pupils and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and were rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. He said the government’s investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, adding that the affected pupils were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were attending to affected pupils at various hospitals. item.title: NEMA Distributes Relief Materials To Gas Seepage-Affected Persons In Rivers Community
item.description: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has distributed relief materials to persons affected by gas seepage in Bille Community, Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State. The intervention, carried out through NEMA’s Port Harcourt Operations Office, is aimed at easing the immediate humanitarian needs of residents affected by the incident. The exercise began with a courtesy visit to the King of Bille Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, King Igbikingeri Ngowari Cornelius. The delegation, representing the NEMA Director-General, Hajiya Umar, was led by Chidi Ogundu, who conveyed the agency’s message of sympathy to the monarch and the people of Bille Kingdom. The delegation later proceeded to Bille Community, where the relief materials were presented to community executives and leaders for distribution to affected persons. The exercise was conducted with measures in place to ensure an orderly and effective delivery of the assistance. Representatives of the Rivers State Emergency Management Agency (RISEMA) and the Nigerian Red Cross Society, alongside other stakeholders, witnessed the distribution. Community leaders expressed appreciation to NEMA and its Director-General for the intervention, saying the relief materials would help ease the hardship faced by residents. They also called for medical outreaches to help identify and address potential health problems associated with prolonged exposure to gas. The gas seepage, which began more than three months ago, is yet to receive a concrete solution from the Federal Government. Investigations into the incident are reportedly ongoing, involving the Federal Ministry of Gas, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), partners and operators. Residents continue to await a lasting solution to the problem and measures to address the potential health risks posed by prolonged exposure to the gas. But we are lucky that this person we know today, without any doubt, is a Ugandan-born person who went to Uganda and she was there for some days. item.title: Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation. But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks. Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday. Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked. item.title: Sowore claps back after Senator Ajibola called him ‘skit maker’
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has hit back at the National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Basiru, after the senator described him as a “skit maker” and “comedian”. Sowore, in a statement posted on X, recalled his longstanding relationship with Basiru, saying they fought against military dictatorship together in the 1990s. He also accused the APC chieftain of abandoning the democratic ideals they once defended because of the privileges of his current political position. The exchange followed Basiru’s appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, where he described Sowore as a skit maker. Responding, Sowore shared a photograph of himself with Basiru taken in 1998, when he led the Congress of Progressive Youths (COPY), a pro-democracy group. “I watched an interview on Politics Today on Channels Television, anchored by Seun Okinbaloye, in which the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, called me a ‘skit maker’ and ‘comedian’,” he wrote. Sowore said he received Basiru at the University of Lagos after the latter was expelled from the University of Ilorin in 1992 over student activism. He said he and other activists, including Kunle Adegoke, popularly known as K-Rad, helped Basiru secure an opportunity to return to the university and study law. “Both eventually graduated with flying colours and went on to accomplish great things,” Sowore said, adding that their shared history made Basiru’s remarks particularly disappointing. He argued that the struggle for democracy and human dignity should not be dismissed as entertainment, insisting that his activism remained consistent with the ideals they defended during military rule. “The struggle for justice, democracy, freedom and the preservation of human dignity is neither skit-making nor comedy,” he said. Sowore also faulted Basiru’s argument that opposition candidates should be ashamed of losing to President Bola Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, which he described as deeply flawed. He maintained that political appointments were temporary and predicted that Tinubu’s administration, like previous military regimes, would eventually leave office. “Political appointments are temporary. Tinubu’s regime will come and go, just like the military regimes we confronted in our youth,” he said. Sowore concluded by accusing Basiru of turning against the ideals he once championed. “What is truly comical is watching yesterday’s beneficiaries of resistance become today’s defenders of the very oppression they once fought against,” he wrote. item.title: Ekiti Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela The Ekiti State House of Assembly has passed the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, seeking to provide for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday, with all 21 members present voting in support, signalling the Assembly’s endorsement of decentralised policing. Following its passage, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Stephen Aribasoye, directed the Clerk of the House to transmit the document to the National Assembly alongside observations made by the state legislature. Speaking on the bill, Aribasoye said state police had remained at the forefront of national discourse for over two decades, noting that the Ekiti Assembly had a historic opportunity to take a position. He stressed the need for effective and responsive security, saying Nigeria’s policing challenges required practical solutions. “Nigerians had repeatedly expressed concerns over delayed responses to distress calls, limitations in operational reach and the distance between law enforcement agencies and the communities they were meant to protect,” he said. The Speaker added that inadequate and poorly coordinated local policing in some areas had contributed to insecurity, threatening livelihoods, disrupting education, undermining business confidence and eroding public trust. He said a properly structured State Police system could strengthen accountability by bringing policing leadership and oversight closer to the people and their elected representatives, subject to constitutional safeguards. According to him, the country could not afford unnecessary delays in addressing security challenges, describing State Police as “a long-overdue practical necessity rather than a mere theoretical preference.” In its report, the Committee of the Whole House recommended concurrence to the bill, subject to an amendment to Section 317A(5). The committee said it considered the bill clause by clause and deliberated on the proposed constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services. It proposed the insertion of the words “an Act of the National Assembly or a Law of the State House of Assembly, as applicable” after the words “this Constitution” in the newly inserted Section 317A(5). The observation, the committee noted, is intended to expressly recognise the legislative authority of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, in authorising relevant security arrangements. item.title: Libya recovers Swiss, Austrian women kidnapped since 2025 in Niger
item.description: Two women — one Swiss and the other Austrian — were released from more than a year of captivity in Niger and arrived in Libya’s eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday. The two women — Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69 — were abducted in Niger in 2025. In a video released by Libya’s eastern-based al-Masar TV, the women appeared emaciated and thanked the country’s eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar and his son, Saddam, for their release. Al-Masar said “two hostages, an Austrian and a Swiss national, have been freed after being held captive in Niger for a year and a half”. “My name is Eva Gretzmacher, I am 76, and I thank from the bottom of my heart Marshal Haftar and his son, Saddam, who released us,” one of the woman said in French. “I had been held hostage for a year and nine months,” she said. Abbt said she was “happy to be free”, also thanking Haftar. Online website Libyan News Observatory also reported their release. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi. Two governments are currently vying for power: a UN-recognised administration in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east backed by Haftar. item.description: Artificial intelligence has found critical security flaws in a major programming language called PHP, with many websites taken offline Thursday as organisations worldwide scramble to fend off would-be hackers. Created in the early 1990s, PHP is a computer programming language that helps run an estimated 70 percent of the world’s websites. It is “a backbone of the web”, according to security firm Wiz Research, which says it used AI to find vulnerabilities hidden in PHP for more than a decade. PHP — a name that originally stood for Personal Home Page — underpins popular web design platforms, meaning the flaws could allow hackers to break into various sites, from online stores to government services. A fix was released Wednesday, with the PHP Foundation telling the tech departments of companies and organisations around the world: “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now.” That has resulted in a slew of apps and websites — from the Paris police website to a Pokemon sleep tracker — going dark as developers work to protect their underlying code from hacks. How did AI find the flaws? Cutting-edge AI models, such as those from US giants OpenAI and Google, were used by Wiz and other groups to uncover PHP’s weak spots in August. This was kept under wraps while a fix was developed. item.title: Ebola: UN expresses confidence in Nigeria’s containment efforts
item.description: The United Nations has expressed confidence in Nigeria’s capacity to contain its newly confirmed Ebola case, pledging support to prevent further spread of the deadly disease. UN Secretary-General’s Spokesperson, Stéphane Dujarric, gave the assurance on Wednesday while responding to questions from the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) at the UN Headquarters in New York. Dujarric said the UN was concerned about the detection of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus in Nigeria, the fifth country to report a case during the current outbreak. However, he expressed confidence in Nigeria’s health authorities, commending their swift response and extensive contact-tracing efforts following the confirmation. “We have full confidence in the ability and the capacity of the Nigerian Government’s health authorities to deal with this single case,” he said. The spokesperson acknowledged that the appearance of the virus in another country raised concerns about its potential spread beyond countries already affected. “Yeah, I mean, it’s of course concerning that there is a case in a new country,” Dujarric said. He, however, noted that Nigerian authorities had already undertaken active contact tracing to identify and monitor people potentially exposed to the infected patient. Asked by NAN whether the UN was worried that the outbreak could spread to additional countries or persist for another year, Dujarric emphasised international cooperation. He urged countries to comply with international health regulations and collaborate closely with the World Health Organisation (WHO) to contain the outbreak. “It is also incumbent that countries work together, follow international health regulations, work with the WHO,” he said. item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of Kano residents in the 2027 general election, expressing confidence that they will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf spoke on Wednesday while representing Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa, Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. The governor also said several projects executed by the Tinubu administration had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that residents of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Umahi Says Economic Hardship Easing Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over, insisting that the Tinubu administration’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts, adding that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road and Zaria-Hunkuyi road projects. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. According to the minister, some inherited projects have been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. Umahi said the Tinubu administration had completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects were ongoing in the region. He added that the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. item.title: Delta traditional rulers mourn Uduaghan
item.description: The Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers has mourned former Governor Emmanuel Ewetan Uduaghan, describing him as a detribalised leader whose legacy of peace, development and support for traditional institutions would endure. The council, in a condolence message dated October 21, 2026, extended its sympathies to the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the people of Delta State over the former governor’s death. The message was signed by the Chairman of the council, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhue I, CFR, MNI. The traditional rulers said the news of Uduaghan’s death was received with shock and profound bewilderment, recalling his cordial relationship with the traditional institution during his tenure as governor. According to the council, Uduaghan prioritised the welfare of traditional rulers and made significant contributions to human capital development, infrastructure and the promotion of peace among the state’s ethnic groups. It described the former governor as a detribalised leader who treated all parts of Delta as one indivisible family, irrespective of ethnic differences. The council noted that although Uduaghan inherited the Warri crisis from his predecessor, he worked to establish lasting peace among the three warring ethnic groups. It said his contributions would continue to resonate among Deltans, particularly his efforts to strengthen the traditional institution and enhance its standing alongside similar institutions in other states. The council prayed for the repose of Uduaghan’s soul and other departed faithful, while asking God to comfort his immediate family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over what it described as an irreparable loss. The council, in a condolence message dated October 21, 2026, extended its sympathies to the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the people of Delta State over the former governor’s death. The message was signed by the Chairman of the council, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhue I, CFR, MNI. The traditional rulers said the news of Uduaghan’s death was received with shock and profound bewilderment, recalling his cordial relationship with the traditional institution during his tenure as governor. According to the council, Uduaghan prioritised the welfare of traditional rulers and made significant contributions to human capital development, infrastructure and the promotion of peace among the state’s ethnic groups. It described the former governor as a detribalised leader who treated all parts of Delta as one indivisible family, irrespective of ethnic differences. The council noted that although Uduaghan inherited the Warri crisis from his predecessor, he worked to establish lasting peace among the three warring ethnic groups. It said his contributions would continue to resonate among Deltans, particularly his efforts to strengthen the traditional institution and enhance its standing alongside similar institutions in other states. The council prayed for the repose of Uduaghan’s soul and other departed faithful, while asking God to comfort his immediate family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over what it described as an irreparable loss. item.title: Yobe court sentences man to death for killing wife
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman A Yobe State High Court sitting in Damaturu has sentenced a 45-year-old man, Abubakar Musa, popularly known as Daddy, to death by hanging for the killing of his wife, Ammi Adamu Mamman. Musa was arrested on January 4, 2024, following his wife’s death at New Bra-Bra Estate, Damaturu, and was subsequently charged with culpable homicide, according to media reports. The then Police Public Relations Officer of the Yobe State Command, DSP Dungus Abdulkarim, said the incident occurred at about 4:48 a.m. on January 4, after the ‘C’ Divisional Police Headquarters in Damaturu received a distress call. Abdulkarim said the couple were on the same bed when Mamman was allegedly attacked with a sharp object on the neck, causing severe bleeding that led to her death. He said Musa was arrested for interrogation, while the homicide unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case subsequently went to High Court 1 in Damaturu, where the judge reportedly held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. University Community Mourned Deceased Mamman’s death also drew reactions from the university community. A February 2024 newsletter published by Yobe State University identified her as a member of staff and said the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mala Mohammed Daura, mourned her death and called on security agencies to ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. The university described her death as a loss to its community. She was buried in Potiskum on January 9, 2024, according to the newsletter. The Women-led Civil Society Organizations Network in Yobe State also condemned the killing and called for justice. In a statement issued shortly after the incident, the network identified the deceased as Ammi Adamu Mamman and said she was a volunteer with one of its member organisations. Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, also expressed condolences to the family and called on security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding her death, assuring that anyone found responsible would face the law. A lawyer quoted in media reports said Musa retained the right to appeal the judgment within the period prescribed by law. Dangote explained that the expansion forms part of a broader strategy to develop an interconnected African energy supply system capable of linking major refining centres with underserved markets that have historically depended on imported petroleum products and fragmented distribution channels. “We are very aggressive with that,” he said, in response to questions about the Group’s plans for petroleum depots, pipelines and logistics infrastructure. He revealed that the acquisition of a 25 per cent stake in Kenya’s petroleum pipeline network was achieved with the support of the Kenyan government and would significantly enhance the movement of refined petroleum products within the East African region. “Just let me tell you, yesterday, with the support from the President of Kenya, we bought 25 per cent of the pipeline network for the distribution of petroleum products,” Dangote disclosed. The Group is also developing a major petroleum distribution corridor linking Djibouti and Addis Ababa, complete with storage terminals and tank farms designed to facilitate the efficient transportation and storage of refined products. He added that another strategic project in Cameroon is nearing completion, while Namibia has been identified as a critical hub in the Group’s plan to penetrate Southern African markets. Dangote described Namibia as a particularly attractive location because of its strategic proximity to the Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos. “From our refinery to Namibia is just about four days of steaming,” he noted. According to him, refined products from the Lagos refinery will be transported to Namibia and distributed across interconnected markets, including Botswana and South Africa. The Group is also examining other supply corridors extending into Zimbabwe and Zambia as part of its broader objective of developing a continental network supported by strategically located storage and transportation infrastructure. The petroleum distribution expansion complements plans to establish another refinery in Lamu, Kenya, with a projected refining capacity of approximately 700,000 barrels per day. Dangote noted that East Africa’s growing economies, vibrant mining sector and increasing energy demand make the region an attractive destination for refining investments. He explained that the proposed refinery would source crude oil from multiple markets rather than depend exclusively on supplies from Kenya or Uganda, ensuring greater flexibility and long-term operational sustainability. According to him, technical assessments identified Lamu as the preferred location because of its deep-water access, marine infrastructure and availability of critical resources required for large-scale refining operations. Dangote revealed that the investment decision was concluded within four months, although he alleged that vested commercial interests attempted to delay the project through legal proceedings shortly before its public announcement. Beyond energy infrastructure, Dangote strongly advocated policies aimed at protecting domestic industries from unfair competition, arguing that industrialisation cannot thrive if emerging African manufacturers are exposed to unrestricted imports from more established economies. He questioned why African countries should be discouraged from supporting local industries when developed economies increasingly deploy similar measures to strengthen domestic manufacturing and employment. Drawing parallels with recent developments in major global economies, he argued that industrial protection remains a legitimate and widely accepted economic strategy. “If America is now saying, no, we are going to protect our industries, who are we in Africa not to protect our own industries?” he asked. Dangote also disclosed that the Group has earmarked approximately $50 billion for investments between 2026 and 2030, describing the programme as part of a broader mission to demonstrate that African businesses can successfully execute transformative industrial projects at scale. “The legacy we are trying to set up is how do we industrialise our continent?” he said. According to him, the investment programme is designed not only to expand the Group’s operations but also to inspire other African entrepreneurs and investors to pursue ambitious industrial ventures capable of reshaping the continent’s economic future. Looking beyond the energy sector, Dangote identified inadequate power supply, weak financial systems and underdeveloped industrial policies as major challenges constraining Africa’s economic growth. He described electricity as a fundamental requirement for industrialisation, particularly in manufacturing, mining and mineral processing, where reliable power is essential for value addition. With an estimated 650 million Africans still lacking access to electricity, he stressed that addressing the continent’s energy deficit would unlock significant opportunities for job creation, industrial development and economic diversification. Questioning why a continent blessed with abundant natural resources, vast arable land and a young population continues to grapple with poverty, Dangote insisted that Africa possesses all the ingredients necessary to become a major industrial powerhouse. item.title: Maradona doctor was made ‘scapegoat’ for his death, court told
item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants. In its closing arguments, the prosecution condemned Luque’s “inaction,” saying his attitude “was always to do nothing” in the face of the warning signs that Maradona was exhibiting. – Contested medical history – Luque’s lawyers particularly attacked the conclusions of the interdisciplinary medical commission, which had been established by the court in 2021 to provide an opinion on the star’s death. The commission, which based its findings on the autopsy and other things, said Maradona had a history of heart problems that should have been taken into account, a conclusion the prosecution emphasized. But Luque’s defense lawyers said that clinical tests done prior to Maradona’s surgery just before his death didn’t reveal any heart issues. “It’s so clear that Maradona didn’t have any heart problems in 2020,” Oneto said during closing arguments.
